newsitem.title: CANADA: Trans Quebec pipeline files for extension to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Trans Quebec pipeline files for extension to U.S..

text.p: Trans Quebec & Maritimes Pipeline said on Thursday it filed an application with Canada's National Energy Board to build a 213-km extension to New Hampshire from Quebec.

The C$270 million extention of the TQM system, co-owned by Gaz Metropolitain & Co LP and TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, would connect with the Portland Natural Gas Transmission System, which was awaiting final U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approval, it said.
TransCanada and Gaz Metropolitain are also partners in the PNGTS project.
Under the plan, the pipeline extension would carry more than 210 million cubic feet of western Canadian gas per day to New Hampshire, Maine and Massachusetts starting in November 1998.
The extension would run to the New Hampshire border, near Pittsburg, from Lachenaie, Quebec, the company said.
